topic: How Does ChatGPT Actually Know What To Say?
title: How ChatGPT Actually Decides What To Say (No, It's Not Thinking)

scenes.text: ChatGPT has never had an original thought in its life. Not one. And once you see why, you'll never look at AI the same way again.
Here's the thing everyone gets wrong. You type a question, it types back an answer, so it feels like it understood you. It didn't. It did math.
Step one: your words get chopped into chunks called tokens. 'Understanding' might become two tokens. The model never sees English. It sees numbers.
Step two: for every single token, the model calculates the probability of every possible next token. All at once. Out of over a hundred thousand options.
Step three: it picks one, usually not even the highest probability one, and does the entire calculation again. One word at a time. That's why it sometimes pauses.
So where does the 'knowledge' come from? Training. It read a huge chunk of the internet and adjusted billions of internal numbers until its guesses matched real text.
So it's not answering you. It's finishing your sentence in the most statistically convincing way it can. That's the whole trick.
If that blew your mind, follow for one of these every week. Next one: why AI sometimes just makes things up.
